temporal_order.statement: NASA remained at FISMA Level 3 across FY 2022-FY 2024.
NASA assigned zero-trust leadership, planned phased corporate implementation, and funded corporate initiatives while mission and JPL owners retained separate responsibilities.
Non-corporate implementation had not begun; legacy systems, distributed ownership, and unknown non-corporate costs remained open.
The later FY 2025 FISMA evaluation again reported Level 3, Consistently Implemented.

dossiers.attribution: NASA OIG independently reports both the implementation condition and the annual maturity result.
dossiers.independent_validation: Independent oversight supplies two different official records; neither report validates a causal link between them.
dossiers.causal_boundary: Temporal order and association may be described; the record does not establish causation.
next_records: Track FY 2026 FISMA results, pillar-level implementation across corporate and non-corporate systems, tested-control operation, incidents, recovery, service effects, and mission outcomes.

temporal_order.statement: DHS moved from ineffective in FY 2021 to effective in FY 2022 and FY 2023.
DHS and CISA continued operating the government-wide CDM program for asset visibility and network monitoring.
GAO identified incomplete guidance, data-quality controls, endpoint onboarding, and cloud-asset management.
DHS OIG rated the FY 2024 department program effective, with function ratings of Level 4 or Level 5.

dossiers.attribution: DHS OIG reports the department result; GAO independently reports CDM implementation constraints.
dossiers.independent_validation: Two independent oversight bodies support the coexistence of the records, not a causal relationship.
dossiers.causal_boundary: Temporal order and association may be described; the record does not establish causation.
next_records: Track FY 2025 department and component ratings, recommendation closure evidence, CDM data quality, endpoint coverage, cloud assets, incidents, recovery, and service effects.

dossiers.entity_name: Department of Health and Human Services

temporal_order.statement: HHS remained Not Effective across FY 2022-FY 2024.
HHS continued department and component remediation under the CIO and FISMA programs.
GAO identified 82 open CIO recommendations, while HHS OIG found supplemental metrics at Ad Hoc maturity.
The FY 2025 evaluation again rated the HHS information-security program Not Effective.

dossiers.attribution: HHS OIG supplies the annual rating; GAO independently inventories open recommendations.
dossiers.independent_validation: Independent oversight confirms both conditions, but open-recommendation counts do not validate the cause of the FISMA result.
alternative_explanations: Control areas outside the open GAO set
dossiers.causal_boundary: Temporal order and association may be described; the record does not establish causation.
next_records: Track FY 2026 FISMA results, recommendation closures, component control testing, incidents, recovery, affected services, and health-program outcomes.

temporal_order.statement: The Phase 56B panel records a company- and MEP-attributed line increase from 40 to 105 units per day.
The company identifies custom engineering, testing, prototypes, and flexible tooling and fixtures as operating inputs.
A proposed 10,200-square-foot expansion is recorded by New York as Cancelled/Declined with $0 disbursed.
No later compatible output, labor, quality, cost, delivery, demand, or WIP observation is publicly exposed.

dossiers.attribution: Current capabilities are company claims; the project status is independently recorded by New York.
dossiers.independent_validation: The state record validates only the public project's status, not the company's operating claims or the reason for the earlier output change.
dossiers.causal_boundary: Temporal order and association may be described; the record does not establish causation.
next_records: Obtain a dated repeat of the same line's output, labor hours, WIP, first-pass yield, scrap, downtime, cost, delivery, and demand.

temporal_order.statement: The acquisition announcement says Island Components would continue operating independently as a G.W. Lisk division.
The current capability profile lists winding, machining, automated equipment, assembly, inspection, environmental testing, and access to parent capabilities.
The public records do not expose utilization, labor, quality, product mix, downtime, delivery, investment, or integration measures.
The later MEP case reports daily output moving from 75 to 120 units, without a repeat observation window.

dossiers.attribution: Acquisition and capability records are company-attributed; the output result remains company- and MEP-attributed.
dossiers.independent_validation: No independent record validates the acquisition's operating effect or the persistence of the reported output change.
dossiers.causal_boundary: Temporal order and association may be described; the record does not establish causation.
next_records: Collect repeated output, labor hours, WIP, first-pass yield, defects, downtime, delivery, and parent-resource use for the same line.

temporal_order.statement: Monaghan describes respiratory-device manufacturing under medical-device and environmental management controls.
The company attained ISO 14001 certification and set continual-improvement, waste-diversion, and emissions-reduction objectives.
No common quantitative series connects the management system to line output, product mix, labor, quality, cost, delivery, waste, or emissions.
The later MEP case reports one line increasing from 6,000 to 9,000 units per day.

dossiers.attribution: Certification and environmental objectives are company-attributed; the output result is company- and MEP-attributed.
dossiers.independent_validation: Certification validates a management-system standard, not the magnitude, cause, persistence, or breadth of operating outcomes.
dossiers.causal_boundary: Temporal order and association may be described; the record does not establish causation.
next_records: Collect same-line output, labor, yield, scrap, downtime, delivery, demand, waste, emissions, and certification-surveillance records.

dossiers.entity_name: Dynegy Moss Landing Power Plant Hybrid

temporal_order.statement: EIA plant code 260 increased from 400 MW in 2021-2022 to 750 MW in 2023.
CPUC conducted an on-site generation audit with equipment inspection, document review, and staff interviews.
The audit identified potential GO 167 violations requiring response and corrective action.
The operator filed dated responses and claimed corrective actions; later regulator closure and battery-specific performance remain unverified.

dossiers.attribution: CPUC attributes the findings; the operator attributes the responses and corrective actions.
dossiers.independent_validation: The regulator file independently validates that findings and responses exist, not the operating effect or durable closure of each item.
dossiers.causal_boundary: Temporal order and association may be described; the record does not establish causation.
next_records: Track regulator closure, later audits, generator identity, duration, availability, incidents, dispatch, revenue, grid service, and reliability effects.

temporal_order.statement: EIA plant code 60014 remained at 409 MW across final 2021-2023 inventories.
The utility placed a 409 MW, approximately 900 MWh battery in service in December 2021 near solar and transmission assets.
Conversion losses, duration, system conditions, cycling, degradation, and rate recovery shape operation.
PSC filings state uses for high load, reserves, transmission constraints, frequency response, and off-peak or solar charging.

dossiers.attribution: The utility supplies the operating descriptions inside Florida PSC proceedings.
dossiers.independent_validation: The regulator docket validates the filing and asset characteristics, but not realized dispatch frequency, value, reliability effect, or cost effectiveness.
dossiers.causal_boundary: Temporal order and association may be described; the record does not establish causation.
next_records: Collect interval dispatch, availability, cycles, state of charge, degradation, revenue, curtailment, outage response, and customer-cost records.

temporal_order.statement: EIA plant code 63834 remained at 250 MW across final 2021-2023 inventories.
CPUC audited Gateway under GO 167-C and required responses to identified safety, maintenance, documentation, and work-management issues.
The audit identified 16 findings requiring corrective action.
Gateway stated that 14 findings were closed and two were targeted for closure by the end of October 2025.

dossiers.attribution: CPUC attributes the findings; Gateway attributes closure status and risk characterization.
dossiers.independent_validation: The regulator file validates the response, not independent closure, durability, safety effect, availability, dispatch, or customer outcome.
dossiers.causal_boundary: Temporal order and association may be described; the record does not establish causation.
next_records: Track CPUC closure evidence, later audits, availability, incidents, dispatch, duration, degradation, revenue, grid service, and reliability effects.

dossiers.causal_boundary: Temporal order and association may be described; the record does not establish causation.
